settings.heading: Liner and Brow Definition in a Single Pencil

settings.text: One pencil, two jobs. The fine matte tip draws a crisp line along the lash for definition, then feathers into short strokes that fill and shape the brow. The formula sets waterproof within seconds and resists smudging, so a morning application still reads clean at the end of the day. Choose from Black and Graphite for a defined look, or Bronze, Brown, Chocolate, Plum and Stone for something softer.

settings.name: Jennifer S
settings.body:
I didn't realise how much I had stopped trusting my own face until I started avoiding photos.

It sounds silly until you've done it yourself.

I'd get ready, spend ages on my eyes, feel really confident walking out the door, then someone would pull out their phone and I'd immediately think about my eyeliner.

Not the photo.

Not how I looked.

My eyeliner.

Was it still even? Had the corner smudged? Was there black under my eye?

Eventually I started checking reflective windows and bathroom mirrors without even thinking about it.

The first few times I thought I was just being picky.

Then I realised I wasn't enjoying getting dressed up anymore.

I was managing my makeup.

Finding something that stayed put changed that more than I expected.

Now when someone says “let's take a photo,” my first thought isn't “wait.”

It's actually just “sure.”

And I didn't realise how much I'd missed that feeling.

settings.name: Holly E
settings.body:
The most annoying thing about bad eyeliner isn't the smudge.

It's what the smudge does to your confidence.

I'd leave the house feeling put together and completely forget about my makeup.

Then I'd see a photo later and suddenly everything I felt good about was gone.

I wouldn't even notice the outfit anymore.

I'd zoom straight into my eyes.

One side looked heavier.

The wing had softened.

There was a little black mark underneath that I somehow hadn't felt happen.

It made me start deleting photos.

Not because I hated how I looked.

Because I hated how unpredictable my makeup had become.

I eventually realised I wasn't trying to find better eyeliner because I loved makeup.

I was trying to find it because I wanted to stop thinking about my makeup.

That difference sounds small.

It isn't.

Now I can actually get ready and move on with my day instead of wondering when my eyeliner is going to betray me.

settings.name: Chloe M
settings.body:
I used to carry eyeliner everywhere.

Not because I was obsessed with makeup.

Because I didn't trust the eyeliner I had on.

There was always this little voice in my head saying, “You should probably check.”

So I'd go to the bathroom.

Look in the mirror.

Fix the corner.

Come back.

An hour later, I'd do it again.

I didn't realise how exhausting that was until I stopped doing it.

The first time I went through a full night without checking my eyes, I actually forgot about them completely.

I was talking.

Laughing.

Taking photos.

Going outside.

Just living.

And then I got home and looked in the mirror.

My makeup still looked like the makeup I'd put on hours earlier.

That was the moment I realised the problem wasn't that I was “too high maintenance.”

I just wanted makeup I could put on and stop managing.

Honestly, that feels so much better.

settings.name: Emma A
settings.body:
I almost stopped doing winged eyeliner altogether.

Not because I stopped liking it.

I stopped liking what happened after I finished it.

I'd spend ten minutes getting both wings symmetrical and then spend the rest of the night protecting them.

Don't touch your eyes.

Don't rub them.

Don't get too hot.

Check before taking a photo.

Check after taking a photo.

It became ridiculous.

Something that was supposed to make me feel more confident had turned into something I was constantly worrying about.

Then I found an eyeliner that actually stayed looking the way I wanted for much longer.

And weirdly, the biggest change wasn't my makeup.

It was me.

I stopped thinking about my eyes every five minutes.

I stopped avoiding close-up photos.

I stopped carrying a backup pencil.

I just wore the makeup and went about my night.

Sometimes the thing you want from a makeup product isn't a more dramatic look.

It's getting your attention back.

settings.text: A matte waterproof formula with a fine tip that works for both liner and brows, in seven shades — where most pencils give you one finish, one job and a line that fades by lunch.

settings.heading: Is it really waterproof?
settings.text: Yes. Once the formula sets it resists water, sweat and humidity, so it holds through workouts, hot weather and teary moments without running.

settings.heading: Can I use it on my brows as well as my eyes?
settings.text: That is what the fine tip is designed for. Use long strokes along the lash line for liner, and short feathered strokes through the brow to fill sparse areas and shape the arch.

settings.heading: Which shade should I choose?
settings.text: Black and Graphite give the most definition. Brown, Chocolate and Bronze suit lighter hair and a softer daytime look. Plum flatters green and hazel eyes, and Stone works as a subtle everyday brow shade.

settings.heading: Will it smudge or transfer onto my lids?
settings.text: The matte formula sets within seconds of application and stays put. Allow a moment to dry before blinking hard or applying other products over the top.

settings.heading: How do I remove it?
settings.text: Because it is waterproof, water alone will not lift it. Use an oil-based or bi-phase makeup remover on a cotton pad, hold it against the lash line for a few seconds, then wipe gently.
